content.tex: This investigation looks at the connections between the rectangles made by dividing one rectangle into two smaller rectangles.
\(\bullet \bullet\) the length of a rectangle is always longer than its width
\(\bullet \bullet\) the length and width of a rectangle are always a whole number of units \(\bullet \bullet\) the scale factor of any enlargement is greater than 1.

content.tex: A rectangle is cut into two smaller rectangles, A and B.
When B is an enlargement of A, the original rectangle is called a \(scale-rectangle\) .
A 4 by 10 rectangle is cut as shown.
\(\frac{length of B}{length of A} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\) and \(\frac{width of B}{width of A} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\)
So B is an enlargement of A with scale factor 2.
This means that the rectangle with dimensions 4 by 10 is a \(scale-rectangle\) with a factor of 2.
